title: SLO Evidence Gating and Capacity Onboarding Canvas
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This canvas documents the SLO evidence gating and capacity onboarding workflow used by SRE to admit new services (or new model tenants) onto production inference capacity. It is intended to be a prescriptive checklist and operational reference for engineers, product owners, and SREs who are preparing a service for live traffic.

Goals:
- Ensure every service has measurable, verifiable SLOs before it draws sustained production capacity.
- Capture and standardize the evidence artifacts required for admission decisions.
- Define the capacity safety and headroom requirements for heterogeneous inference workloads.
- Provide a repeatable sequence (gating) to reduce regression risk while onboarding.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all services using the Redwood inference runtime in hosted, dedicated, or private deployments.
- Includes new services, major model-version rollouts, and tenant onboarding where capacity is non-trivial (>= 0.5 GPU sustained).
- Not intended for experiments under short-lived dev/test clusters (those follow the dev-cluster checklist).

Key definitions:
- SLO: Service Level Objective (primary SLOs: p99 latency <= target_ms; availability success_rate >= target%).
- Evidence artifact: concrete telemetry, traces, and synthetic canary results demonstrating an SLO is met under expected load.
- Admission gate: a checklist item that must be satisfied (or waived with approver) to move to the next phase.

Admission gates (high level):
1) SLO specification approved: owner declares the SLOs (metrics, aggregation windows, burn window) and the target thresholds.
2) Telemetry & dashboards in place: metrics, traces, and SLI pipelines present and validated.
3) Synthetic canary and load profile: canaries executed for the expected P95/P99 token paths and latency distributions.
4) Capacity headroom analysis: provisioning plan with headroom >= required% and pre-warm strategy.
5) Degradation & fallback plan: documented fallbacks, circuit-breakers, and prioritized tenant lists.
6) Post-admission validation run: 24–72 hour monitored validation with SLOs asserted and a positive retro.

Detailed gating checklist (explainers and acceptance criteria):

A) SLO specification (owner: service/product engineer)
- Must include: metric name (as emitted), SLI aggregation (per-minute counters vs histograms), SLO target, measurement window, burn-rate alert thresholds.
- Required primary SLOs for inference services:
  - Latency p99_over_request (sliding 1h): target <= 250ms (default for interactive reads).
  - Success rate (5xx and explicit failure signals): target >= 99.9% over 1d window.
  - Token generation throughput SLO (for heavy batch tenants): 99th percentile throughput >= committed qps on provisioned pool.
- Acceptance: SLO page with canonical metric queries and calculated current baseline (see sample PromQL below).

B) Telemetry & observability (owner: service/SRE)
- Metric coverage: latency histogram, request counters (by outcome), queue length, GPU utilization (per-pool), host OOM events, memory pressure, and GPU memory fragmentation.
- Traces: end-to-end trace that links client request -> gateway -> serving runtime -> model stage. Include KV cache hit/miss spans.
- SLIs implemented as production queries with alerts:
  - Example PromQL: rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference",le="0.25"}[5m]) / rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="inference"}[5m]) to estimate proportion under 250ms.
  - Error rate query example: increase(http_requests_total{job="inference",code=~"5.."}[1h]) / increase(http_requests_total{job="inference"}[1h])
- Observability acceptance: dashboards render with live data, test traces in staging replicate the production trace structure.

C) Synthetic canary & load profile (owner: eng+dex)
- Canary types: functional, latency, burst, and long-tail token simulation.
- Scenario matrix: build at least three scenarios representing 1) typical interactive traffic, 2) peak burst (3x typical qps sustained for 2 min), 3) worst-case long sequence (2x tokens per request, high memory).
- Canary execution plan:
  1. Run baseline canary in staging (smoke and trace verification).
  2. Run canary against a shadow/provisioned pool in prod with traffic mirroring at 1–5% for 30–60 minutes.
  3. Run synthetic load up to expected on-ramp and validate tail latency and error rate.
- Acceptance: p99 latency within 1.2x of target in mirrored runs; no unhandled 5xx spikes; KV cache hit rate documented.

D) Capacity headroom & allocation (owner: capacity planning/SRE)
- Required artifacts: capacity plan, provisioning script or Terraform changes, autoscale policy (min/max), pre-warm/warm-pool strategy.
- Default headroom requirement: 40% spare capacity above expected peak for new model tenants on heterogeneous GPU pools. For single-tenant dedicated pools negotiate separately.
- Admission requires: evidence of prescriptive autoscaler policies and a validated pre-warm sequence (examples below).
- Stress validation: a controlled ramp to 75% of provisioned capacity for 1 hour with SLOs holding and with the autoscaler simulated (or observed) to behave as expected.

E) Degradation and fallback plan (owner: service/SRE/product)
- Must include: graceful demotion policy (e.g., fall back to a smaller/or quantized model family), token-priority routing, and an emergency capacity escrow list of low-priority tenants to be evicted.
- In-run actions mapped to triggers:
  - If sustained SLO burn rate > 3x for 15m -> immediate demote to fallback model via routing policy.
  - If GPU OOMs > 5 across pool in 10m -> soft-evict low-priority background batch jobs.
- Acceptance: documented playbook with runbook links and explicit owner for each action.

F) Post-admission validation (owner: SRE)
- Observe the service in production for 24–72 hours under expected traffic. Collect SLO metrics, incident evidence, and a short retro.
- Post-admission checklist: no unexplained p99 increases, error budget burn within predicted margin, trace samples reviewed.
- Failure modes: if SLOs degrade beyond allowed 1.5x target, trigger rollback to previous model/config and open an incident.

Required evidence artifacts (deliverables):
- SLO page (single source of truth) with queries and thresholds.
- Dashboard snapshots and links (latency histogram, error rate, pool utilization).
- Canary logs and trace IDs (include at least 5 representative traces).
- Capacity plan (numbers, cost estimate, TF plan link).
- Degradation playbook (runbook ID and owner contact).
- Post-admission retro notes and mitigation tickets.

Minimum telemetry retention and fidelity requirements:
- Raw request-level traces: retained for 7d with 100% sampling for canary windows and 0.5% sampling for regular traffic.
- Aggregated SLI metrics: 30d retention at 1m granularity, 365d retention at 1h granularity.
- Storage and access: evidence must be accessible to SRE and owners for audit; include links in the admission doc.

Operational playbook snippets and commands:
- Trigger a mirrored canary (k8s job): kubectl apply -f test-canary-mirror.yaml -n sandbox
- Run stress generator (example): siege --concurrency=200 --time=60s --url "https://mirror.example/run?seq=long"
- Example Prometheus alert snippet (yaml):
  - alert: InferenceP99Breach
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"inference\"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.25
    for: 15m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      runbook: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/inference-p99-mitigation

Decision authority and waivers:
- Default: Admission requires approval from the service owner, SRE reviewer, and capacity manager.
- Waivers: an approver can waive a non-critical gate for time-boxed experiments (48h) but must document compensating controls.

Ownership and contacts:
- SRE reviewer: oncall-sre@redwood.ai (primary), secondary: Marcus Chen.
- Capacity manager: capacity-team@redwood.ai.
- Product/Service owner: must be declared on the SLO page.

Escalation and rollback triggers (examples):
- Immediate incident and rollback if: p99 latency > 2x target for 30m OR error rate > 5% for 15m.
- On-call escalation: page SRE primary -> SRE lead -> service owner.

Example acceptance template (to paste into admission request):
1) SLO page link: <link>
2) Dashboard snapshots: <links>
3) Canary run IDs and traces: <list>
4) Capacity plan link: <link to TF / runbook>
5) Degradation runbook ID: <runbook link>
6) Post-admission validation window: planned_start / planned_end
7) Approvals: [service_owner], [sre_reviewer], [capacity_manager]

Related runbooks and references:
- inference-p99-mitigation runbook (operations)
- model-hotpatch-and-rollback-procedure (emergency)
- capacity-onboarding-checklist-for-new-model-tenants (capacity planning)

Revision history and notes:
- 2024-09-15: initial draft created by Aisha Patel.
- 2024-11-02: tightened default headroom from 30% to 40% after cross-pool instability exercises.
- 2025-02-20: added PromQL examples and expanded posterior evidence retention policy.

Appendix: sample PromQL queries and alert text:
- p99 latency (histogram_quantile): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"inference\",service=~\"<service>\"}[5m])) by (le, instance))
- error rate: increase(http_requests_total{job=\"inference\",service=~\"<service>\",code!~\"2..\"}[1h]) / increase(http_requests_total{job=\"inference\",service=~\"<service>\"}[1h])
- GPU utilization (per-pool): avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent{pool=\"<pool>\"}[5m])

If you are preparing an admission request and need a reviewer, ping oncall-sre@redwood.ai with the subject: "Admission request: <service> SLO gating" and attach the required artifacts.
